relations.name: invoice_record
relations.meaning: One billed-revenue invoice as recorded in authoritative billing sources, keyed by invoice_id referent.
relations.grounding_contract: Every tuple must cite sources/billing/invoices.json row for invoice_id with field-level pointers for billed_name, amount, currency, period, and status.
relations.construction_rule: C1: Parse invoices.json; mint referent invoice:<invoice_id>; assert one tuple per invoice with values copied exactly from source fields.

relations.name: crm_account_record
relations.meaning: One CRM account row as recorded, keyed by crm:<crm_account_id> referent.
relations.grounding_contract: Every tuple must cite sources/crm.csv row for crm_account_id with field-level pointers.
relations.construction_rule: C1: Parse crm.csv; mint referent crm:<crm_account_id>; assert one tuple per row with values copied exactly.

relations.name: registry_company_record
relations.meaning: One company-registry row as recorded, keyed by registry:<company_number> referent.
relations.grounding_contract: Every tuple must cite sources/company_registry.csv row for company_number with field-level pointers.
relations.construction_rule: C1: Parse company_registry.csv; mint referent registry:<company_number>; assert one tuple per row with values copied exactly.

relations.name: contract_header
relations.meaning: Contract identity and counterparty naming as stated in an authoritative contract file, keyed by contract:<filename-without-.md> referent.
relations.grounding_contract: Every tuple must cite the matching sources/contracts/*.md file with pointers to the header fields and counterparty line.
relations.construction_rule: C1: For each contract markdown file, mint referent contract:<stem>; extract document_kind, counterparty_name, effective_date, and governing_law from the header block without semantic reinterpretation.

relations.name: contract_stated_expiry
relations.meaning: An explicit expiry or non-renewal statement recorded in a contract source, when the text states one.
relations.grounding_contract: Tuples with non-null expiry_date or non_renewal_stated=true must cite the exact contract text span stating expiry or non-renewal; contracts without such language have no tuple.
relations.construction_rule: C1: Parse contract files for explicit Expiry/expires/non-renewed language; copy stated date text and whether non-renewal is explicitly recorded.

relations.name: contract_section_excerpt
relations.meaning: A verbatim excerpt of a labeled contract section used to ground later clause-presence judgments.
relations.grounding_contract: Every tuple must cite sources/contracts/*.md with section heading and copied excerpt text.
relations.construction_rule: C1: Segment each contract file by markdown section headings; store section_label and excerpt text without paraphrase.

relations.name: legal_form_name_variant
relations.meaning: A documented mechanical legal-form spelling variant between two name strings (e.g., Ltd versus Limited) that sources treat as the same registered form.
relations.grounding_contract: Each tuple must cite an authoritative source observation of both strings or a documented registry/legal-form rule applied to observed names.
relations.construction_rule: C1: Emit only exact legal-form variants evidenced in sources or commercial_notes.md; do not generalize beyond observed pairs.

relations.name: contract_clause_present
relations.meaning: Whether specific contractual language of a given clause_kind appears in the authoritative contract text, independent of any acquisition or dependency policy.
relations.grounding_contract: Accepted or rejected tuples must cite contract_section_excerpt spans or equivalent contract file pointers; unresolved tuples record insufficient or ambiguous text.
relations.construction_rule: C2: For each contract and clause_kind in {change_of_control_consent, change_of_control_termination, assignment_consent, assignment_notice, assignment_affiliate_exception, assignment_competitor_prohibition, exclusivity, auto_renewal_term, rolling_term}, judge presence from section text.
relations.candidate_generation_rule: Cartesian product of compiled contract referents with the fixed clause_kind enumeration; skip pairs already resolved for the current revision.
relations.unresolved_judgment: Whether the contract text contains language matching the clause_kind definition.

allowed_dispositions.REJECT: present=false with supporting excerpt or explicit silence where the section addresses the topic
allowed_dispositions.UNRESOLVED: text is ambiguous, incomplete, or insufficient to assert presence or absence

relations.name: contract_lifecycle_status
relations.meaning: Whether a contract is active or expired according to stated dates, explicit expiry/non-renewal language, and recorded term structure in sources.
relations.grounding_contract: Every resolved tuple must cite contract_header, contract_stated_expiry, and/or contract_section_excerpt evidence for the active or expired determination.
relations.construction_rule: C2: Judge status as active or expired from effective dates, stated expiry, and explicit expired/non-renewed statements; do not apply purpose-specific inclusion filters.
relations.candidate_generation_rule: One candidate per compiled contract referent.
relations.unresolved_judgment: Whether source dates and term language establish the contract as currently active or expired.

allowed_dispositions.ACCEPT: status=active or status=expired with cited evidence
allowed_dispositions.REJECT: not used; absence of confident lifecycle judgment is UNRESOLVED
allowed_dispositions.UNRESOLVED: dates or term language do not support a confident active/expired classification

relations.name: entity_identity_judgment
relations.meaning: Purpose B epistemic judgment linking two prescribed identifier endpoints as the same legal counterparty, distinct parties, or unresolved.
relations.grounding_contract: SAME_ENTITY and DISTINCT tuples require evidence from CRM, billing, registry, contract, and/or legal_form_name_variant observations; UNRESOLVED records examined evidence without a confident positive or negative judgment.
relations.construction_rule: C2/C3: Resolve identity_link_candidate pairs under Purpose B policies; emit disposition SAME_ENTITY, DISTINCT, or UNRESOLVED using identifier forms crm:, billing:, registry:, contract:.
relations.candidate_generation_rule: Derived from identity_link_candidate; do not assert pairs outside the Purpose B required link topology.
relations.unresolved_judgment: Whether two commercially relevant records refer to the same legal counterparty.

relations.name: invoice_counterparty_association
relations.meaning: Purpose A judgment whether an invoice billed name and a contract counterparty can be confidently linked for exposure reporting.
relations.grounding_contract: Asserted tuples require confident linkage evidence across billing and contract sources, optionally supported by entity_identity_judgment; unresolved tuples record candidate association without confident join.
relations.construction_rule: C2/C3: For each invoice_contract_association_candidate, judge asserted only when billed_name and contract counterparty are confidently the same party; otherwise unresolved. Never treat missing linkage as proof of non-association.
relations.unresolved_judgment: Whether invoice billed_name and contract counterparty_name refer to the same counterparty with confidence sufficient for Purpose A.

allowed_dispositions.REJECT: not used; uncertain linkage is UNRESOLVED, not a negative association finding

relations.name: commercial_dependency_assertion
relations.meaning: Purpose C judgment that a counterparty-contract pair is commercially dependent under Purpose C rules or remains unresolved because identity or join evidence is insufficient.
relations.grounding_contract: Dependent tuples require resolved identity joins, open_invoice or active rolling/auto-renewal evidence, and contract_clause_present obligation kinds; unresolved tuples cite blocking identity or join uncertainty.
relations.construction_rule: C2/C3: For each dependency_evaluation_candidate, assert dependent only when current-relationship and obligation-kind predicates are confidently satisfied and required identity joins are resolved; otherwise unresolved. Do not emit a negative dependent=false world fact.
relations.unresolved_judgment: Whether the counterparty-contract pair satisfies Purpose C dependency criteria given invoice openness, contract lifecycle, obligation clauses, and identity joins.

allowed_dispositions.REJECT: not used; failing criteria or unresolved joins yield UNRESOLVED rather than a false dependency

relations.name: identity_link_candidate
relations.meaning: A directed pair of Purpose B identifier endpoints that must receive an entity_identity_judgment to connect CRM, billing, contract, and registry candidates for a commercial relationship.
relations.grounding_contract: Derivation inputs are compiled WORLD records; completeness receipt must name the commercial-relationship universe used to generate required links.
relations.construction_rule: C4: SQL/Python over crm_account_record, invoice_record, registry_company_record, contract_header, and legal_form_name_variant to emit the Purpose B required link topology only.
relations.candidate_generation_rule: Enumerate relationship-spanning endpoint pairs per Purpose B required_link_topology; exclude pairs with no commercial nexus.

relations.name: invoice_contract_association_candidate
relations.meaning: An invoice-contract pair whose billed name and contract counterparty may correspond and therefore requires a Purpose A association judgment.
relations.grounding_contract: Derivation inputs are invoice_record and contract_header; completeness receipt must name the invoice and contract universes.
relations.construction_rule: C4: Join invoices to contracts when counterparty naming or identity evidence creates a candidate commercial nexus; include unresolved-association invoices that may qualify under Purpose A coverage rules.
relations.candidate_generation_rule: Emit candidates where billed_name and contract counterparty_name share mechanical variants or fall within the same commercial-relationship cluster suggested by sources.

relations.name: open_invoice
relations.meaning: Invoices whose billing status is recorded as open in authoritative billing sources.
relations.grounding_contract: Each tuple derives from invoice_record with status='open' and inherits that row's billing grounding.
relations.construction_rule: C4: SELECT invoice FROM invoice_record WHERE status equals the source-recorded open status literal.

relations.name: dependency_evaluation_candidate
relations.meaning: A counterparty identifier and contract referent pair that Purpose C must evaluate for commercial dependency or unresolved status.
relations.grounding_contract: Derivation inputs include contract_header, open_invoice, contract_lifecycle_status, contract_clause_present, and entity_identity_judgment; completeness receipt must name the candidate universe.
relations.construction_rule: C4: Emit counterparty-contract pairs that may meet Purpose C criteria because of open invoices, active auto-renewing or rolling contracts, or unresolved identity joins that block evaluation.
relations.candidate_generation_rule: Cross eligible contracts with Purpose B counterparty identifiers linked through resolved or candidate identity paths and open-invoice relationships.
